A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PRISM study. Their full text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison despite reformatting, relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original MUSE and WMDP experiments, jailbreak and relearning evaluations, component ablations, and parameter and layer studies.

after.justification: V2 retains these empirical results and adds comparator evaluations, attack-size studies, an isolated component ablation, runtime measurements and representation-margin measurements.

M1.justification: The adversarially trained probe, harmless-class loss, parameter smoothing and retain-gradient projection remain unchanged. Algorithms 1–2 match between v1 Appendix B and v2 Appendix C. Expanded probe explanations and newly disclosed settings do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: The MUSE-Books/News, WMDP, dialogue-training, safety-attack and utility-benchmark coverage is retained. New margin and attack-size studies reuse MUSE-Books; their sample-size variations change evaluation settings within existing coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds actual evaluations of RMU and RMU-LAT on MUSE-Books, including unlearning performance in Table 16 and relearning comparisons in Tables 4 and 18. V1 cites the underlying work but does not evaluate these baselines. These add directly relevant representation-based and latent-adversarial alternatives while retaining the earlier comparators.

E3.justification: V2 adds 100- and 200-example relearning evaluations at 50 and 100 steps, a margin protocol using 100 forget examples, and component timing with 2048-token inputs. Original benchmark metrics, model configurations, selected epochs and attack-step grids remain unchanged. The newly documented 400-example attack cap does not establish a change to earlier experiments.

E4.justification: V1 ablates PS, GCD and RS together with GCD; v2 Table 5 additionally removes RS alone, isolating its contribution. V2 also adds attack-sample-size sensitivity, component runtime attribution and direct probe-margin measurements in Tables 4 and 15–18. Existing parameter and layer analyses are retained.

E5.justification: V2 Appendix F.11 newly states that a fixed random seed selects the 100 margin examples, without supplying its value. Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new median and tenth-percentile margins summarize examples, not uncertainty across runs.

E6.justification: The original primary scores remain unchanged, including PRISM's Table 1 scores of 0.860 on Books and 0.522 on News. V2 adds substantial results for RMU/RMU-LAT, smaller relearning datasets, isolated RS removal, component runtimes and margins. For example, new Table 17 reports median margins of 0.852 for PRISM and 0.728 for SAM+NPO. These extend the evidence rather than demonstrate improved original-setting performance over v1.

T1.justification: V2 adds the formal unlearning setup in Section 3.1 and refines assumptions supporting the existing derivations. Appendix D.1 explicitly places the entire perturbation ball inside the smooth neighborhood; D.2 adds differentiability, Lipschitz-gradient and radius conditions. The FGSM/SAM derivations and gradient-projection argument otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central proposal and claims: dual-space smoothness and gradient-conflict decoupling improve robustness and balance forgetting, utility and privacy. The additional experiments support these retained claims without redefining the core contribution.

C2.justification: V2 clarifies how model updates satisfy the robust probe, interprets the new margin and runtime findings, and explicitly describes bounded black-box and white-box threat models. Appendix J newly acknowledges the absence of a formal guarantee that combining the smoothness objectives produces synergistic robustness. Earlier over-refusal and training-complexity limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 Appendix E.2 newly specifies masked mean pooling, probe perturbation magnitude 0.01 and adversarial-loss weight 0.4; the MLP architecture was already in v1's pseudocode. It also documents RMU/RMU-LAT settings, runtime input length and attack resources. The first-page footnote now advertises data alongside code at the existing repository. These mainly expand documentation.

R1.justification: V2 adds Thaker et al. (2025) and Łucki et al. (2024) to support adversarial evaluation and threat-model positioning, while removing the Dou et al. (2024) and Ni et al. (2025) citations. The broad positioning relative to unlearning, probes and SAM remains intact; much related work is relocated.

P1.justification: V2 condenses the main related-work section and moves its detailed discussion to Appendix B, adds preliminaries and an additional-studies subsection, and places limitations last. Selected introduction and method paragraphs are rewritten, and acknowledgements and conference headers are added. Most prose and the overall narrative sequence remain recognizable.

P2.justification: V2 adds five tables, expands the component-ablation table and corrects the swapped VerbMem/KnowMem headings in v1 Table 13, now Table 14. The conference layout substantially resizes and reflows displays and adds shaded PRISM rows. Existing plots and the workflow figure are retained; the changes extend beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: The isolated RS ablation resolves v1's combined-removal ambiguity, while RMU/RMU-LAT comparisons and margin/runtime studies strengthen specific empirical support. Added probe settings improve reproducibility, and explicit assumptions and the acknowledged lack of a synergy guarantee improve precision. These provide a focused strengthening of the existing paper; the principal results remain unchanged and repeated-run uncertainty remains unreported.
